event_confirmation: Company-announced (GlobeNewswire 2026-10-01 'Carpenter Technology Announces Conference Call and Webcast'; local report https://www.mychesco.com/a/news/regional/carpenter-technology-sets-oct-22-earnings-update/ dated 2026-10-05/06): fiscal Q1 FY27 (quarter ended 2026-09-30) results released BEFORE the market opens Thursday 2026-10-22, call 10:00 ET. Session bmo is CORRECT. The sweep's 'historically amc' note is wrong: the Oct-23-2025 release was also before the open (https://www.mychesco.com/?p=640759). So the baseline's history, tagged amc off 8-K acceptance times, records the DAY-AFTER moves, not the reactions: the real bmo reactions were Oct-23-2025 about +20% intraday (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/10/23/why-carpenter-technology-stock-is-soaring-today) and Jul-30-2026 about -5.4% (MarketBeat, via https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/carpenter-technology-nysecrs-issues-quarterly-earnings-results-2026-07-30/). The baseline's own volume check flagged the Oct 2025 row as bmo with a +22.66% move.
conviction_note: The number comes from abs_move 9 and p_up 55. The guide-implied Q1 EPS (~$3.10 at the $195-200M operating income guide) sits a little above a $3.00-3.04 consensus. The CEO called the $850-880M FY27 guide a floor. GE Aerospace raised its guide on Oct 20 with supplier material input up double digits. The stock has de-rated 40% from its high on target cuts, with no estimate cuts found. Against that: 4.3 points of put skew, $54M of net insider selling, and a July EPS beat that sold off 5.4%. So the lean stays small, and impact_sum (+2.2) sits above the scaled number because each finding is sized alone.
bar: Consensus Q1 FY27 EPS $3.00 / revenue $828.7M (OpenCapital, via search snippet) and $3.04 / $829.56M (MarketBeat figures quoted at https://www.ad-hoc-news.de/boerse/news/corporate-news/carpenter-technology-stock-gains-before-october-22-results/70227860). Company guide: Q1 operating income $195-200M (SAO $218-222M, PEP $6-7M, corporate ~$29M), FY27 operating income $850-880M, adjusted FCF $400-430M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000017843/000001784326000030/a4thqtr2026resultspressrel.htm, 2026-07-30). Two estimate sources agree within $0.04 and a company guide exists, so the bar is sourced. Scaling Q4's $3.23 EPS on $206.9M operating income gives ~$3.08-3.12 at the Q1 guide, about 2-3% above consensus. The stock trades on the FY27 operating income guide and SAO margin.
positioning_check: Short interest: ~1.5M shares, 2.6 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 FINRA settlement (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/crs/short-interest/); 'just under 3% of free float' per Ortex 2026-10-14 (https://ortex.news/articles/188164/crs-analysts-cut-targets-sharply-as-stock-slides-to-380). That is not crowded. No October settlement was found. Options (baseline): event-implied move 12.9%, 25-delta skew +4.34 vol points (downside paid), put/call OI 0.43, but total OI is only 1,779 and the ATM spread is 18.8% of mid, so the chain is thin. Tape: -6.6% over 20 days, -40.4% from the $625.99 52-week high, about -35% since the July 30 print. 20-day realised vol is 19.6% against 57% ATM IV.

findings.finding: GE Aerospace (the largest engine OEM and a direct customer tier for CRS superalloys) reported Q3 on 2026-10-20, after CRS last spoke. It raised 2026 guidance across the board (op profit to $10.9-11.0B from $10.55-10.75B) and said 'material input from priority suppliers' rose double digits YoY. Total engine deliveries rose 8% and LEAP 5% in Q3 (26% YTD). This corroborates the A&D volume behind CRS's $218-222M SAO guide and the 'engine customers capacity-constrained' comment from CRS's July call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CRS's A&D-driven beat plus raise in Oct 2025 bought about +20%. In Jul 2026 A&D sales rose 17% with an EPS beat and a new FY27 guide, and the stock fell 5.4%. The line has paid in both directions.
findings.why_not_priced: It came out two sessions before CRS's print, and CRS still drifted to $368.8 (-2.9% over 5 days) after it. If the market had read it through, CRS would have firmed with GE rather than kept falling. The derating looks multiple-driven (target cuts, rates), not demand-driven, so counterparty demand evidence is not what the price is pricing.
findings.independence: Proxy (counterparty, not CRS's own number). Same direction: Boeing Q3 deliveries of 161 jets with 124 737s (https://boeing.mediaroom.com/2026-10-13-Boeing-Announces-Third-Quarter-Deliveries) and an Argus 2026-08-03 report that engine OEMs significantly raised H1 deliveries, lifting melter demand.

findings.finding: RTX Q3 2026 (8-K, Oct 2026): Pratt & Whitney commercial OE sales fell 5% YoY, while commercial aftermarket rose 21% (GTF) and total P&W sales rose 10%. That is a mixed read for engine OE alloy pull, the second engine OEM after GE.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No CRS-specific history of reacting to P&W OE; CRS reports A&D as one line.
findings.why_not_priced: Public days before the print and small. It matters only as an offset to the GE read, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: None from a different source. Partly offsets the GE finding; spares and aftermarket demand also consume CRS alloys, so the net is near zero.

findings.finding: Boeing delivered 161 commercial jets in Q3 2026 (124 737s, 22 787s), 475 YTD (release 2026-10-13). On the July call CRS's CEO said 'some structural customers remain cautious in their ordering patterns' and that recovery depends on Boeing's ramp. A strong delivery quarter supports the structural and fastener orders CRS flagged as ramping.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not separable from the overall A&D line in CRS's history.
findings.why_not_priced: Public on Oct 13, and CRS fell after it. A secondary source says Boeing's CEO acknowledged in September that stabilising at 47/month is taking longer, which caps this. Sized small as a proxy.
findings.independence: Secondary summary https://migflug.com/afterburner/?p=27994844 (rate 42/month, 47 delayed) cuts partly against it. GE finding above is a different document pointing the same way on engines.

findings.finding: The Q1 FY27 guide of $195-200M operating income (reduced by elevated Q1 preventative maintenance) implies EPS of about $3.08-3.12, using Q4's $206.9M operating income to $3.23 EPS and ~49.6M shares after buybacks. That sits slightly above the $3.00-3.04 consensus. Track record: Q4 FY26 landed at $206.9M inside a $205-210M guide; Q1 FY26 beat the $2.13 consensus at $2.43.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jul 2026: EPS $3.23 vs $3.08-3.09, revenue $851M vs $863.3M, and the stock fell ~5.4%. Oct 2025: EPS $2.43 vs $2.13, revenue missed, and the stock rose ~20%. Revenue has missed consensus on the last two prints, so the EPS line alone has not been paid reliably.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it sits inside what the company told the market to expect, so it is sized near zero. Consensus below the guide midpoint suggests the street haircut the guide for maintenance and leaves a small beat cushion.
findings.independence: Shares a document with the LTA finding (the July call). Q4 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000017843/000001784326000030/a4thqtr2026resultspressrel.htm gives the Q4 base.

findings.finding: On the July 30 call CEO Thene said a large LTA renewal is under negotiation, that other significant contracts come up over the next two years, and that price will be 'a big driver' in FY27. He also said 'if investors treat [the $850-880M FY27 guide] as the floor, you wouldn't get any pushback from me.' The Q1 call is the first chance to announce the renewal or raise or firm the FY27 range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY26: the initial $660-700M guide (Oct 2025) was raised over the year to $700-705M and landed at $702M. The Oct 2025 print with the guide came with +20%. The July 2026 FY27 guide plus a FY29 $1.2-1.3B target came with -5.4% (a CEO death the same week confounds it).
findings.why_not_priced: Price targets were cut 25-30% in October (JPM 700 to 520, TD Cowen 650 to 500, KeyBanc 608 to 465) while ratings stayed at Buy/Overweight and no estimate cuts were reported. The market is applying a lower multiple and is not visibly paying for a guide raise or LTA pricing. If it were, the stock would not be -35% since the guide was given. Whether the renewal lands in this window is uncertain, hence the wide band.
findings.independence: Same transcript as the guide-implied EPS finding. No independent second source on the LTA.

findings.finding: The stock has de-rated about 40% from its $625.99 high (spot $368.8) and about 35% since the July print. Sell-side cut targets sharply in October (JPM 700 to 520 on 10-14, TD Cowen 650 to 500 on 10-09, KeyBanc 608 to 465 on 10-08, Wells Fargo to 430) but kept positive ratings. Ortex describes these as valuation revisions ('what that business is worth at current market conditions') with no fundamental cut. Short interest is ~3% of float, about 2.6 days to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Oct 2025 print after a quieter tape: +20%. July 2026 print after a run to highs: -5.4%. A low bar after a drawdown has preceded the larger positive reaction on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Expectations have reset on the multiple, not the numbers, so a print at or above the guide is measured against a de-rated price. The +4.3 skew argues the option market still pays for downside. Reasons it may be wrong for this print: the chain is thin (OI 1,779, 19% spread), and peer HWM's derating came from a GE-in-sourcing scare (GE buying CPP castings, Sep 2026) rather than from demand. Sized small for being against the skew.
findings.independence: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/crs/ lists the same target cuts. Sector context: HWM fell ~11% on GE's CPP purchase (https://www.tikr.com/de/blog/howmet-aerospace-stock-dropped-nearly-11-after-ge-bought-a-rival-casting-supplier-heres-whether-the-selloff-is-an-overreaction).

findings.finding: CEO Tony Thene sold over 34,900 shares at $479-489 in late August without a 10b5-1 plan (>$10M), weeks after giving the FY27 guide, and net insider disposals were ~113,000 shares (>$54M) over the 90 days to Oct 6, with no purchases.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance tied to a print found.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is public in Form 4s and was cited in September commentary on the slide. It is filed because a discretionary CEO sale after setting a guide is a signal about how much upside management sees near term.
findings.independence: Tickeron 2026-09-10 (https://tickeron.com/blogs/carpenter-technology-crs-falls-18-1-in-30-days-despite-record-earnings-16521/) also cites the late-August CEO sale and >$40M of 12-month insider selling. It shares the Ortex document with the positioning finding but is a different fact.

findings.finding: In August 2026 CRS repurchased the remaining $119.0M of its $400M program (211,565 shares, about $562 average per the 10-K) and authorised a new $1.0B program on 2026-08-11, more than twice the old one. The Q1 release will disclose Q1 buybacks, possibly accelerated at prices now 35% lower; the FY27 FCF guide is $400-430M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None separable; buyback disclosures have accompanied each recent print.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorisation is public. The pace bought under it in September at the lower prices is not, and a heavy pace would read as management buying the drawdown, the opposite signal to the insider sales.
findings.independence: 10-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000017843/000001784326000034/crs-20260630.htm confirms the subsequent-event repurchase and shows 49,558,566 shares outstanding at 2026-08-07.

findings.finding: Non-aerospace segments were weak into the quarter: on the July call Medical was -30% YoY (+5% sequentially) and Energy -12% YoY. FY26 Medical was -21% as the medical supply chain manages inventory closely (10-K). That is a drag on revenue against a ~$829M consensus, while Industrial & Consumer was +22% on semiconductors. A&D is ~65% of sales and grew 15-17%, which outweighs these lines.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue missed consensus on the Oct 2025 and Jul 2026 prints; the reactions were +20% and -5.4%, so the revenue line has not decided the reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Known segment trends. Filed small because revenue consensus has been too high on two straight prints, so a third revenue miss is a modest risk. Sized net of the A&D majority.
findings.independence: July call transcript https://www.webull.com/news/15319831763051520 gives the quarterly segment figures.

outside_window.finding: GE Aerospace's pending acquisition of Consolidated Precision Products (castings) brings an alloy-consuming casting operation under an engine OEM. It may shift negotiating power in future superalloy LTAs, but nothing about it resolves in this print.

The brownfield expansion is on schedule for early FY28 (July 2027 onward), and the FY29 operating income target is $1.2-1.3B. These are long-dated drivers that do not resolve in the window except as reaffirmations.

baseline_tension: The evidence leans slightly long (counterparty strength, a guide called a floor, an expectation reset with no estimate cuts), which cuts against the +4.3 put skew and the -40% drawdown. So p_up is held at 55 rather than 60, and the findings that rest on the reset are sized small.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 / core (finding inside the guided range): the guide-implied Q1 EPS beat cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Rule 7 (sign against the skew): the positioning/derating long cut from +1.0 to +0.7 with an explicit reason the thin chain may be wrong; p_up from 56 to 55
Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; July EPS beat sold off 5.4%): the LTA/guide-floor finding cut from +0.8 to +0.6

'A reaction history built from the wrong events': the amc-tagged baseline moves were rebuilt from confirmed bmo reactions (+20%, -5.4%); abs_move_pct kept at 9 between that history and the thin 12.9% option implied move
Rule 5 (proxy evidence): GE, RTX and Boeing kept as small proxy findings with independence stating so; left unchanged
